objections.claim: A stale line in the Explicit-deferrals list still reads 'authoritative-closure/replay halves of DR-106/109/113', contradicting the entry's own two 'deferred WHOLLY' statements and re-creating exactly the hazard MF-03 withdrew.
objections.evidence: Amended entry, Explicit-deferrals paragraph (file line 420): '…Windows platform support, baseline/ratchet, authoritative-closure/replay halves of DR-106/109/113.' Versus the State paragraph (lines 401-406): 'DR-106, DR-109 and DR-113 are deferred WHOLLY: their acceptance-evidence cells all begin with applied DR-002..008 successors…', and the condition-2 set (lines 430-432): 'DR-106, DR-109, DR-113: deferred wholly (MF-03)'. The Explicit-deferrals list is the operative enumeration of what receives recorded dispositions ('each gets its recorded disposition, never silence'). A disposition author following the list would scope the three dispositions to the authoritative-closure/replay halves — reinstating the unlawful split, and leaving the non-authoritative remainder neither affected nor disposed: silence, which the entry's own header rule and condition 2 both forbid. D-001's adopted doctrine (turn-2 NOTE-1 / ADV-D001-T2-05) is that checklist text and register must never disagree; the same discipline applies to an entry disagreeing with itself.
objections.proposedFix: Replace the list item with 'DR-106/DR-109/DR-113 (each WHOLLY — MF-03)'. One line.

objections.claim: The coordinator's turn-2 message states the baseline/ratchet trade was recorded ('your axis-6 objection adopted with the trade recorded'); the amended bytes record the conditional-revisit rule but not the trade. In a PREFERENCE-LADEN entry decided on the user's behalf, the register must show the user what was traded, and a coordinator report must not outrun the bytes.
objections.evidence: Amended entry lines 406-410 record: OUT of slice 1; slice-2 revisits first if DR-006 lands binding fingerprint recipes; 'recorded so the product value is deferred, not forgotten'. Nowhere in the entry is the trade itself stated — that conditional inclusion would couple slice-1 ship to the evidence-identity lineage head landing binding recipes, versus exclusion shipping `analyze` sooner without the prototype's net-new-findings CI workflow (prototype-evidence-reference.md, Baseline/ratchet row). D-000 clause 5 makes preference-laden overturn procedures cost less than the decision; the user can only exercise that cheaply if the register shows what the preference traded. The report-versus-bytes discipline is the corpus's own: freeze §7.1's correction narrative records the exact failure mode of converting a lane report into a claim about bytes.
objections.proposedFix: Add one clause to the baseline/ratchet sentence naming the trade, e.g.: '(trade: conditional inclusion would couple slice-1 ship to the DR-006 lineage landing binding recipes; exclusion ships analyze sooner without the prototype's net-new-findings CI workflow)'. Alternatively record in the Reviewer line that the trade lives in the turn-1/turn-2 review artifacts by digest.

objections.claim: Three turn-1 NOTEs were accepted per the coordinator's message but have no corresponding edits: ADV-D002-09 (G06/G11 labeled not-slice-1-required), ADV-D002-10 (each scoped inclusion — DR-105, DR-124, G08, G09, G19 — lands as a recorded scope disposition, not register prose), ADV-D002-11 (overturn-cost decay boundary once dependent commits land). Acceptance without implementation should say where each accepted instruction now lives, or the acceptance is only conversational.
objections.evidence: The G06/G11 sentence and the Overturn line are byte-identical to the pre-amendment draft; no scoped-inclusion-disposition commitment appears. Non-blocking by the turn-1 grading, and NOTE-level items may lawfully be absorbed into later work — but then the entry (or the adoption-time Reviewer line) should record that routing, in the same way D-001 recorded NOTE-1 as 'adopted as a standing instruction'. This NOTE also carries the ADV-D002-04 residual sliver: the DR-110 deferral disposition, when authored, should draw the DR-107/G18 generation-rollback versus DR-110 self-update-rollback boundary and note that file 02's core-inventory 'updates' entry is unexercised in slice 1.
objections.proposedFix: Either implement the three one-liners now, or add to the Reviewer line at adoption: 'turn-1 NOTEs 09/10/11 accepted as standing instructions on the deferral-disposition and adoption commits' — naming where each will be discharged.

objections.claim: In the Identity-dependencies section, the route-B consequence is explicit only for SARIF ('drops from slice 1 by that disposition's terms'); for the other four rides — cache/regeneration keys, subjectScopeCommitment, PlanId/typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, observation→faultCause — the consequence of a scoped-disposition closure is inherited but unstated, and three of those four sit under the slice's core `analyze` command rather than under a severable feature.
objections.evidence: Amended entry lines 371-383. A DR-006 route-B closure that keeps subjectScopeCommitment or the PlanId digests unsettled blocks blueprinting of `analyze` itself, not an optional projection. The entry's framing survives — condition 1 completes first, each disposition names what may be designed, and the slice presumes nothing — so this is structurally sound and non-blocking; but symmetry would make the section complete.
objections.proposedFix: One sentence after the list: 'The same conditional applies to every ride above: a scoped-disposition closure binds the dependent surface — for the non-SARIF rides that surface is analyze's own design — by that disposition's terms.'
